description: One of the standard adornments available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: White-Gold Eyeshadow
description: This mystic eye-shading is a favorite of members of the Mages Guild, as it makes their eyes resemble the guild's famous magic-eye symbol. Enchanting!

name: Winter Princess Glamour
description: Applying this shimmery azure glow to your face tells everyone that you are a princess and are worthy of all the good things in life. What are those good things? Up to you, of course, because you're a princess!

name: Woodsman Goatee
description: One of the standard adornments available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Adamant Dwarven Senche
description: There have long been unconfirmed reports of Dwarven Senche vamidiums with key parts made of the extremely rare and super-hard Dwarven Adamant metal. At long last, these reports have been substantiated.

name: Akaviri Potentate Sabre Cat
description: "Mirannah of Gwylim writes 'the Potentate sabre cat mounted regiment combed Skyrim for Reman loyalists in 2E 7'—potentially accurate. But I think she meant 'killed Solitude's wolves using magical roars' to be local myth."—Honorata Ancrus, Eyevea

name: Anka-Ra Senche-Lion
description: A combination of feline agility with the power of a sandstorm makes this mount both a favored and feared battle companion of the eternally loyal Anka-Ra warriors.

name: Ashbone Sabre Cat
description: "Yes, this one will do nicely. As vengeful and accursed as my master. It bears the mark of Malacath well—our enemies will cower before us! May it lap the blood of its prey on the broken path we ride."—Ogmash the Mighty

name: Ashgray Senche-Serval
description: "House Mornard won't say where it tamed these gorgeous beasts. My guess is Summerset. For a time, only the elder nobles of that house rode their own. Now, after a downturn in Mornard fortunes, you'll find them all over Tamriel."—Sadia Vonius, Student

name: Auric Sabre Cat Duskstalker
description: "Duskstalkers hunt and gather tormented battlefield ghosts, providing these lost souls a safe haven until they willingly leave. They can be seen as wisps, whose colorful auras emanate around both the sabre cat and its rider."—Clever Woman Moritra

name: Baandari Pedlar Senche-Lion
description: Prone to rumbles and purrs, the Baandari Pedlar Senche-Lion serves as both a mount and a source of warmth on cold evenings around the campfire. Just watch out for that rasping tongue.

name: Battlefield Nightmare Senche
description: This intimidating horned senche steed wears coal-black barding, making its orange flames stand out in stark contrast. Though none know its origins, the touch of the Deadlands looks to be upon this mount, making it favored by Mehrunes Dagon's adherents.

name: Black Forge Iron Senche
description: Born from the same wretched forges as Dark Anchors, these ebony-alloy senche atronachs manifest in a burst of soul-searing light when called. Though onlookers may feel as if they'll never be warm again, some riders claim they feel nothing while mounted.

name: Black Fredas Ashen Sabre Cat
description: With the chaos and mischance of Black Fredas on your side, you're sure to cause quite a stir when you pass through town—none wish to catch the eye of your Ashen Sabre Cat lest they fall under its curse!

name: Black Fredas Senche-Lizard
description: Some find the color unnerving, but many riders enjoy the onyx shade and welcome the superstitious tales that follow this mount. Just know that countless legends and tales of woe begin when a Black Fredas beast crosses one's path.

name: Black Mane Lion
description: At the Palace of the Mane near Torval, by tradition the Bi-Lunar Guard are all mounted on matching Black Mane Lions, which are reserved for them alone. So be wary if you ride your Black Mane near Torval, lest you anger the Bi-Lunars!

name: Black Senche-Lion
description: The legendary preferred mount of Elsweyr's greatest thieves, the most famous Black Senche-Lion of all was Rajhin's mount Umbrage, which could both talk and, for brief periods, fly!

name: Black Senche-Panther
description: A mount said to have been bred by Baandari Pedlars for ease in hastily leaving town after dark.

name: Blazeborn Senche-lion
description: Born in flame, this senche-lion's temperament matches its fiery appearance. Those who earn its respect, however, gain a mount that can blaze a path through the darkest shadows.

name: Blessed Highmane Lion
description: "And thus did Alkosh bestow a companion of pure light upon his champion. From atop the beast, the champion rode a noble path. And wherever the lion's paws fell, light and justice soon followed thereafter." —Path of the Highmane, translated

name: Bloodroot Wild Hunt Senche
description: Bloodroot senches revel in the gore of their rider's battle fury, making them excellent steeds for those who love bloodlust as much as the Dreadhorn clan does. Will you embrace this partnership of slaughter?

name: Carnaval Jaguar
description: Jaguar riders may find themselves thirsting for something other than wine as they stalk Carnaval feasting grounds on these stately and suave mounts. Good thing these felines are silent as the shadows.

name: Cat o' War Senche Lion
description: "Like Spriggans roam the glades on land, so does this creature prowl around the tidepools. Its gnarled wooden bones sprout with aquatic life. If it sees me, I'm sure it'll tear my throat out."—Scrap from the lost journal of Teldh

name: Celestial Lynx
description: Swift as a stream and silent as a shadow, this creature appears in many folktales across Tamriel. In some, the lynx stalks its quarry across the night sky. In others it's an agile companion, perfect for worthy hunters prowling the darkest nights.

name: Chilling Senche-Lizard
description: "This Chilling Senche-Lizard is quite rare; it comes from very deep in the swamp, from a tribe said to be dedicated to Frost spells as a means of living longer by living slower. Their Hist tree even drips with icicles (whatever they are)!" —Ukaspa

name: Cinder Skeletal Senche
description: "Long-held grudges and rage simmer within this skeletal senche—fitting given its supposed origin as a battle steed for Orcs fighting within the Ashen Forge! This mount's riders gain the utmost respect from Malacath's adherents."—Erisa Moorcroft

name: Clouded Senche-Leopard
description: A strong yet nimble mount, bred for hunting in the Tenmar forest.

name: Culanda-Born Senche
description: "This steed's glow comes not only from its Culanda-enhanced barding but also from an interaction between it and the animal. Culanda is in its blood—state various Nenalata Ayleid writings—giving this senche envious grace."—Beredalmo the Signifier

name: Cursebound Sabre Cat
description: The roar of a sabre cat bridled by a deathless curse shreds a soul to pieces, or so say those at the Bards College in Solitude. Yet that doesn't deter ambitious necromancers from trying to tame these frightening creatures.

name: Cursebound Sabre Cat Prowler
description: This creature is dominated by the oppressive energies of Coldharbour, bound to its master by a vile pledge to Molag Bal. Though it lacks the ability to act without command, the simmering rage bottled inside the beast grows with every passing day.

name: Cyan Dwarven Senche
description: "The Dwemer of old are known for their clever inventions. Here, they've captured the likeness of a senche through ingenious carving and materials. All these years later, the creature still easily heeds its master's call."—Dwarven Constructs: A Guide

name: Dark Brotherhood Sabre Cat
description: Few creatures are more apt mounts for the Dark Brotherhood than sabre cats. Light on their feet, agile, and with a hunting instinct to match their rider's, many Dark Brotherhood members believe a sabre cat mount is a gift from Sithis himself.

name: Dark Delirium Senche
description: "There is madness in all of us, and senches don't commit to anything half-heartedly. I came across one such mad senche and still bear the scars of its wild attacks. To take one on an adventure, you'd have to be mad as Sheogorath himself!"—Vi Aspblade

name: Death Mask Sabre Cat
description: Most inhabitants of Skyrim hate and loathe necromancy, but those Nords who do stoop to raising the dead tend to go all in, wallowing in death and its symbols. It was no doubt such Nord necromancers who bred the skull-faced Death Mask Sabre Cats as mounts.

name: Dragonscale Barded Senche
description: "Our distant cousins, the senche-mounts, look so majestic in Dragonscale Bard, like creatures who've just stepped out of an ancient wall-frieze in Dune. Perhaps these pesky Dragons have a use after all, yes?" — Master Groom Zarbi'dahuz

name: Dragonscale Frost Senche
description: According to the notebooks of Corvus Direnni, the frost senche-panther may actually be a form of atronach summoned from a plane known as the Fourth Sinus of Takubar. Why it remains in Tamriel where it willingly submits to the orders of mortals is unknown.

name: Dro-m'Athra Senche
description: The Senche-shaped dro-m'Athra are known to the Twilight Cantors as the sar-m'Athra, but everyone else just calls these eerie and uncanny mounts the Dro-m'Athra Senche.

name: Dunecoat Senche-Serval
description: Originally found in the arid canyons of Northern Elsweyr, these striped beauties rarely submit to training, making cats that do extremely desirable. Just make sure to have plenty of toys on hand or you'll find your leather boots gnawed to pieces.

name: Dwarven Senche
description: Since nearly all Dwemer sites are in northeast Tamriel, where the only large feline is the sabre cat, scholars of Dwarven civilization have long wondered why they chose to make animunculi mounts that resemble the senche-tigers of the south. It's a mystery!

name: Ebon Dwarven Senche
description: Certain rare Dwarven senche vamidiums are constructed with key mechanical components forged, not of the usual Dwarven metal, but of ebony and ebony-steel alloys.

name: Falkreath Riding-Lynx
description: The people of Falkreath call these lynxes "blizzard bringers." The cats are as powerful as the buffeting winds that scour the slopes of the Shriekwind Bastion. There are even rumors that the lynx's growl causes avalanches high up in the mountains.

name: Flame Atronach Senche
description: For centuries the conjurers' standard spell for summoning Flame Atronachs has been Koron's Peremptory Summons, which is easily modified to change both the duration of the summoned atronach's binding and its form—for example, into that of a senche-tiger.

name: Frost Atronach Senche
description: Most sorcerers scoff at the idea of imbuing the lumbering frost atronach with feline grace, but when summoned correctly, this frigid senche more than matches its warm-blooded peers in quiet and cunning. Perfect for a hero of your stature!

name: Frost Draugr Senche
description: What were senche-tiger mounts doing in ancient Skyrim, and why were their half-frozen bodies mummified beside the Draugr in certain dark Nord catacombs? And why are they rising now, imbued with animating frost magic? The answers are as yet unknown.

name: Frostbane Sabre Cat
description: Sabre Cats, of course, are inured to the harsh, wintry conditions of Skyrim, and scarcely need warding from the cold; kitting them out as Frostbane mounts is therefore more a question of tradition than of protection.

name: Frostbreak Tiger-Lynx
description: "Keep it well-fed and you'll be fine. It's a smart beast, it won't scratch or run off if it knows you'll give it an easy meal. Just watch your rations on the mountains, though. They're practically invisible in the snow."—Stablehand Skagurn

name: Gloomspore Senche
description: "When developing my Gloomspore Senche, I utilized thunder fungi—a remarkable mushroom that erupts into spores with a deafening boom! I thought it only fitting to mix one roar with another." — Mage Naleldil

name: Green-Graht Ghost Cat
description: The Psijic monk who created the spell for conjuring the spirit of a Psijic Senche Exemplar back into the world of the living as a tangible Ghost Cat was a Wood Elf—which probably explains why it manifests as an Y'frren spirit of the Green.

name: Grinning Terror Senche
description: "This lithe feline possesses the quiet madness of a clever assassin, making it a harmonious steed for those methodically ending the lives of others. Even better—mine sometimes brings gifts of mangled Mer. Perhaps you'll be so lucky?"—Mother Regrets

name: Harvestleaf Lynx
description: "When trees shrug off their colorful mantles, druids gather around a lynx summoned by Y'ffre. While they sing chants, the God of Song and Forest transforms the feline into a steed. Only a Hearthfire champion may claim such a mount."—Book of the Leaves

name: Highland Spotted Lynx
description: This spotted lynx was an uncommon sight in the Colovian hills until an enterprising hunter brought back some young to raise. Decades later, these lithe creatures serve well as mounts to those who prefer felines.

name: Hollowjack Flame-Skull Senche
description: Conventional wisdom holds that these bizarre and eerie Skull mounts are just senche-panthers imbued with a haunting illusory appearance—but some whisper that they aren't from Tamriel at all, but summoned from the Hollowjack half-world or demiplane.

name: Hollowjack Rider Senche
description: Jaque o' the Hollow haunts Rivenspire during dark Witches Festival nights, and even those who ride senche-tiger mounts may find themselves padding headless through the moonless dark while waving a glowing gourd.

name: Indigo Senche-Panther
description: Originally bred for a reclusive family in Rivenspire, the Indigo Senche-Panther possesses a distinctive black fur that has a purple sheen. Rumors claim that when left to its own devices, it stalks werewolves for amusement.

name: Iron Atronach Senche
description: Stories tell of how Maalanrie Direnni, though restrained by bandits, somehow walked through dreams and called the first Iron Atronach Senche. Upon arrival, it destroyed her cage and freed her so she could kill her captors and flee upon its molten back.

name: Karth River Sabre Cat
description: Deep in the Karth River canyon, this golden sabre cat jumps from rock to rock on sparkling spring mornings. Knowing this, young Reach witches often camp nearby to set up their taming rituals, hoping to gain one as a loyal mount.

name: Karthstalker Sabre Cat
description: The dramatic black and white coloration of this lithe mount makes for striking entrances. Watch out, though! Karthstalkers show affection by trying to groom your face.

name: Khefrem Senche-Serval
description: To those living in Hew's Bane, seeing a spotted senche-serval is an omen of good luck. Some, hoping to gain a constant supply of good fortune, captured and trained several cubs. Now they serve as mounts—good luck indeed to those so blessed with one!

name: Kynbound Senche-Panther
description: Known as steeds of the Dremora, Kynbound Senche-Panthers have found their way into service as mounts for those who have some ties to the Dremora. Perhaps that's you?

name: Legion Zero Sabre Cat
description: After forcing sabre cats to drink the Blood of Coldharbour, Legion Zero soldiers mounted up and secured the Imperial City Nobles District for Mannimarco. Many of these soldiers died, leaving their steeds without riders. Perfect—for you, anyway.

name: Manelord Nightmare Senche
description: King of the Nightmare Pride, this night-black senche-tiger has burning paws and flames hissing from its face; rumor says Mehrunes Dagon is responsible.

name: Meridian Sabre Cat
description: "Some accounts of Meridia's plane of the Colored Rooms describe a menagerie of light-imbued spectral beasts elevated from Nirn and 'purified' by the Lady's holy light." —Sayings of Valasha

name: Mirrormoor Shard Senche
description: The armor on this gleaming senche isn't just for its own protection. It's a necessary barrier between the rider and the knifelike shards that cover the beast's body. With time, a patient rider can learn where it's safe to touch the beast.

name: Necrom Armiger Senche
description: "We were all surprised when this senche arrived via envoy. 'A gift from Necrom to an armiger of great repute. Return and aid in the training of more!' And so I ventured to Necrom with a cunning, furry companion."—Armiger Tharys's Journal

name: Nenalata Ayleid Senche
description: "Hunters among the Nenalata Ayleids teamed up with senche mounts daily to track and kill game to help feed the evacuees. King Dynar joined them, riding Ceydarre; he fed her from his own rations."—Beredalmo the Signifier

name: New Moon Senche
description: "Senche steeds are already quiet. This one? It moves as if it is the avatar of silence."—Jonnet of the Sunwalkers

name: Nightfall Sabre Cat
description: The Reachmen of the upper Karth valley, who train them as mounts, swear that the Nightfall variant is sacred to the Daedric Prince Nocturnal. Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.

name: Nighthaunt Gloomspore Senche
description: "I named these senches Nighthaunts because, I suspect, the cult of Vaermina curiosities I was studying during their creation affected their appearance and intensified their glow. Not their nature. Grim-looking they are, yes, but not evil."—Mage Naleldil

name: Nightmare Senche
description: A night-black senche-tiger with burning paws and flames hissing from its face: this is surely the stuff of evil dreams. The origin of this horrific mount is obscure, but some see the hand of Mehrunes Dagon in it.

name: Noble Riverhold Senche-Lion
description: The pastoral tribes of northern Anequina need reliable mounts upon which to follow their herds of livestock, and none are more dependable than the prides of senche-lions bred near Riverhold, feline steeds so brave and loyal they're called "Noble."

name: Oleander Senche-Serval
description: The artists of Black Heights found a new canvas upon which to share their imagination: senche-servals. The high-quality pigments used on this feline's fur weather much without causing harm, and artists claim the cats preen as they're painted.

name: Order of the Lamp Lion
description: "Magicka depleted. Enemies on all sides. The cornered mages despaired. Until they heard a growl erupt into a roar as a Lamp Knight and his leonine steed smashed through the enemy ranks."—Tale of the Palatinus, translated

name: Pellitine Scorch Senche-Lion
description: After the Scorch of Senchal and nearby areas, several prides of senche-lions moved into the area. Enterprising and desperate Khajiit trained some of these fearless creatures to saddle, hoping to bolster their forces against deadly Dragons.

name: Piebald Senche-Serval
description: "Ride one of these piebalds for any travel outside Sentinel. They love the heat more than any senche-serval I've stabled. Makes me believe the tales of Summerset outcasts raising them out in one of the bandit caves nearby decades ago."—Burhan, Stablehand

name: Plague Husk Senche
description: "Some argue that nothing good came from the Llodos Plague, but I disagree. Ride this noxious necromantic senche, and you'll quickly find all the Peryite followers in a crowd. Perfect if you're hunting one down."—Sondryn Fyr, Assassin

name: Plagueborn Senche-Panther
description: Riders of these senche-panthers often find their welcomes worn out while in town, but their journeys across wilderness can be strangely trouble-free.

name: Potentate Halcyon Senche
description: "Having ridden this ephemeral senche, I see why Mirannah insists they are spirits. Her origin date of 2E 29 doesn't match another's 2E 35—either could be true. Regardless, its roar calls forth magic, making it a memorable ride!"—Honorata Ancrus, Eyevea

name: Pride-King Lion
description: The Pride-King Lions are the top predators on the savannahs of Northern Elsweyr. No one but the Khajiit, with their feline intuitions, could have persuaded these proud beasts to serve as mounts.

name: Psijic Senche Exemplar
description: The Psijic Senche Exemplar is the ultimate physical expression of feline grace and power. Khajiiti say it reminds them of the descriptions of Southpaw, the legendary mount of Rajhin the Purring Liar.

name: Ragebound Sabre Cat
description: "When you're at your worst—when the only thing keeping you going is pure rage? That is the moment you know its strength. These cats will happily teach you this lesson, if you need a tutor."—Arparnagh of Markarth

name: Reefborn Senche-Lion
description: "Mages Guild scholars think someone creates these types of senches. With what magic, I don't know. Maybe some sea-loving druid? Regardless, they're as fierce as you'd expect for a senche mount."—Saissula, Stablemaster

name: Sabre Cat
description: The sabre cats of northern Tamriel are possibly even more powerful than their southern Senche cousins. They are certainly more feral and difficult to train. Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.

name: Sabre Cat Frost Atronach
description: A Frost Mage of Clan Direnni spent her entire life perfecting a spell to permanently summon a Frost Atronach in the shape of a Sabre Cat. (Why? Who knows? Balfiera Island is a strange place.)

name: Sagacious Psijic Senche
description: The Psijic Order has bred these senches for centuries, selecting only the brightest among the litters to sire the next generation. Psijics who choose them as companions often form telepathic bonds and claim they are wonderful conversationalists.

name: Sapiarchic Senche-Serval
description: "As the Sub-Sapiarch of Domestic Livestock, I was assigned by Larnatille to breed an appropriate mount for our sages to ride upon when working in the field. I proudly present my result: the loyal and majestic senche-serval!" —Corderil of Sunhold

name: Senche of Scarlet Regret
description: This ominous companion, conjured by Psijic magic in the shape of a glowing senche mount, represents for the monks of Artaeum all of the painful choices they regret having made, but which they nonetheless must ride upon into the future.

name: Senche-Cougar
description: The cliffs and escarpments of east central Elsweyr are the home of the nimble and sure-footed senche-cougars, who prowl the rocks hunting goats and marmots. Inevitably, they've been domesticated by their feline cousins the Khajiit.

name: Senche-Leopard
description: A mount bred for bearing an armed warrior while slinking through the steamy jungles of Pellitine.

name: Senche-Lioness
description: These fierce and powerful mounts hail from the broad savannahs of Anequina.

name: Senche-Lizard Steed
description: "More than once I have been asked, 'Ukaspa, why are your lizard-steeds shaped like mounts from other parts of Tamriel? Why aren't your so-very-handsome mounts shaped like, well, lizards?' These are good questions!" —Ukaspa of Lilmoth

name: Shadow Atronach Senche
description: Summoned from Oblivion, this shadow atronach was made all the more grand by being compelled to take the form of a senche mount. It's popular amongst those who wish to move quickly and quietly through the more dangerous realms of Tamriel.

name: Shadow-Rider Senche
description: Creatures of "Shadow"—are such things possible? Or is the Shadow-Rider Senche merely a black senche-panther mount wrapped in Illusion spells? Somehow, it just seems too uncanny for that mundane explanation.

name: Shadowcap Cave-Senche
description: "Ahzidal made the shadowcap's azure glow the centerpiece of this unsettling feline mount. Prized by spelunkers, this luminescent mount can light up the darkest caverns without making a sound. "—Halund Greycloak

name: Shadowghost Senche
description: An oversized breed of black senche-panthers, the Shadowghost Senche is said by the Khajiit to be sacred—or rather unholy—to Namiira the Great Darkness, who sends them as mounts to bear away those who are doomed to die.

name: Silver Rose Senche-Serval
description: The Knights of the Silver Rose spent years finding the best felines to rid their fortress of pests and annoyances. Generations later, and these senche-servals can clear out banekin infestations in a single day.

name: Skeletal Senche
description: The Skeletal Senche may be the most fearsome of all feline mounts. Expertly re-animated, even in undead form it retains all the lithe strength it possessed in life.

name: Snow Leopard Sabre Cat
description: The shamans of the Skaal tribe domesticated the Snow Leopard Sabres as mounts, but to keep them exclusive their breeding was restricted, and they are down to a dwindling few. Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.

name: Snowclaw Senche-Serval
description: "People say you should be wary of shadows, but what about blinding white snow? When you get disoriented in a blizzard, when you can't tell up from down anymore, that's when the snowclaws will strike! I can feel it."—Last journal entry of Hunter Keedru

name: Snowy Sabre Cat
description: Of all Tamriel's great felines, the Snowy Sabre Cat is the hardiest when it comes to winter weather, barely noticing the Atmoran gales as they come howling in across the Sea of Ghosts. Riding Skill does not affect this mount's appearance.

name: Soulrazer Senche
description: Plates of armor hover around the nonexistent fur of a blue senche. It makes no noise—does not growl or roar with the thrill of the chase. It creeps across the ground slowly, knowing that no prey can escape once the hunt has begun.

name: Sovngarde Valorfang Sabre Cat
description: "Lithe sabre cats are prized among Sovngarde's heroes, particularly those called valorfangs, who died while defending their riders. They stand ready at the Hall of Valor, waiting to convey a hero to a warrior in need of aid."—Clever Woman Moritra

name: Star-Born Guardian Senche
description: Senches are opinionated creatures, but ones imbued with the confidence of the stars are infinitely more judgmental than their Nirn-born counterparts. Riding one of these across Tamriel is a clear sign that even the stars heed your power.

name: Starchaser Senche
description: "Celestial senches prowl over jagged rocks on surprisingly soft paws for creatures made of Spellscar-like stone. Yes, the Steed constellation is a horse, but how the Warrior didn't ride a starry senche into battle is beyond me."—Madadi, Celestial Scholar

name: Stonelore Lynx
description: "It may be a little biased of us, but predators take longer to earn their horns. I suppose we just want proof that they're well-trained before we give them another weapon. Still, little Ivy was so proud when she got hers."—Druid Celina, Beast Master

name: Storm Atronach Senche
description: It is said the great conjurer Corvus Direnni was the first to compel a Storm Atronach to assume the form of a great cat, and shocked all Balfiera Island by riding around its shores on a crackling Storm Atronach Senche!

name: Striped Senche-Tiger
description: A semi-domesticated version of the wild senche-tiger, this distant relative of the Khajiit has been bred for size and manageability.

name: Sunspire Champion Senche-Lion
description: Those skilled enough to overcome Sunspire can earn a special variant of the Sunspire Ice-Fire Senche-Lion. With golden armor and gear, this mount shines, reflecting your own adventuring glory.

name: Tenmar Senche-Tiger
description: Deep in the shadows of the Tenmar Forest, hidden by its camouflaged coat and stealthy stalking, the Senche-Tiger is a nearly invisible jungle predator. Even as a mount, it retains something of the air of mystery it wears in the wild.

name: Tharn's Lucent Revelry Senche
description: "Trust the Tharns to find a way to make a senche even more regal than it already was. I feel underdressed. Do you think it outranks me?"—Legionary Liodes Salvius

name: Umaril's Radiance Senche
description: "Nomads of the sands traded with the Unfeathered's foes. 'Let us disrupt them with mounts both fleet and quiet.' The desert cats I worked with adapted quickly. May they forever slip through the silence for him."—Gandravanya's Journal, Translated

name: Vale Sabre Cat Growler
description: Bards in Skyrim claim these luminous sabre cats gain their glow from Kyne. Scholars in the College of Sapiarchs refute this, each with their own pet hypotheses. Everyone agrees that this growler's fur is silky soft and its rumbling purr soothing.

name: Verkarth Senche-Lioness
description: This sleek and light-hued mount hails from Verkarth, where some warriors drill both night and day to earn the right to train a young one as a battle mount. Now more widely available, you too can add one to your stable.

name: Vitrine Dwarven Senche
description: "When considering the Dwarven automaton mounts, the so-called vamidiums, one gets the sense that the Deep Elves were not attempting to replicate nature, but to improve upon it. Case in point: the Vitrine Senche." —Thelwe Ghelein, Scholar of the Dwemer

name: Volcanic Senche-Panther
description: This molten mount radiates heat and reeks of brimstone. Some Dark Elves swear that it emerged from the heart of Red Mountain itself, but they speak of this only in whispers. Those who seek such a blasphemous steed will find none better!

name: White Lion
description: In Elsweyr, the White Lion is considered a highly prestigious mount. When King Keirgo married Queen Eshita, his Orcrest Honor Guard, twenty strong, were all mounted on mature White Lions.

name: Wild Hunt Senche
description: The Wild Hunt unravels the shapes Y'ffre established for creatures in the Dawn Era, transforming them into monstrous but vigorous hybrid beasts. Among these, both beautiful and abhorrent, is the Wild Hunt Senche-Mount.

name: Wildburn Lynx
description: "To follow the Dawnway requires faith. We are returning to our roots—to the old magic that the Wild Elves used. You can't expect it to be without its share of weeds. Still, the Green provides."—Priest Nothelas, Vashabar

name: Wraithtide Senche
description: "Some believe these skeletal senche respond to the call of a lost soul seeking safe passage. I firmly believe Y'ffre's hand is involved, and I pray I can prove it one day."—Druid Phillic

name: 10-Year Anniversary Golden Wisp
description: Celebrate the 10-Year Anniversary by dancing in the golden light of this summoned wisp.

name: Amaranthine Pocket Watcher
description: "My notes indicate these vibrantly hued watchers once inhabited the ruins of Zaintiraris until an unfortunate explorer set them free. Given their color and origin, I suspect Sheogorath holds some sway over them. Also unfortunate."—Warlock Aldaale

name: Ancestor Moth Swarm
description: "The Ancestor Moths that accompany some mystically-attuned mortals are more than mere insects—they are animated by the loving spirits of the dearly departed, and may grant wisdom and awareness to those they visit." —Sister Terran Arminus

name: Baby Netch
description: Once this young Netch calf imprints on a master, it will follow him or her anywhere, floating along and tootling happily.

name: Bitter Coast Wasp
description: "My family thinks wasps are the worst, but one of these solitary fellows helped me stave off a cliff strider attack. It started following me after it nibbled on a strider I'd killed. I guess it likes to eat them."—Gellius Nuncius, Wanderer

name: Blue Dragon Imp
description: "A 'Baby Dragon,' you say? No such thing. What you have there is a clever Illusion Imp that's found a way to get free handouts and a warm place to sleep. Young folk these days: so gullible." —Divayth Fyr

name: Blue Shock Nixad
description: The rare and colorful Shock Nixad looks rather like a tiny, winged Storm Atronach, though without the whirling electric rocks. They make loyal companions—though they may also make your hair stand on end!

name: Blue Torchbug
description: The night before Waking Day, Iliac Bay Bretons share stories about the Terrible Torchbug of Molag Bal. While the story varies, all agree on one thing: those followed by a cobalt-hued torchbug possess a savagery in battle that haunts any who survive.

name: Bright Moons Dragon Imp
description: "A very talented Imp, no? It cannot be denied Jone and Jode have blessed this creature with their light. Some even speak of having to hide their moon sugar from it!" —Adept Lakjo

name: Bright Moons Lunar Moth
description: "When a Bright Moons Lunar Moth follows you, the blessings of Jone and Jode flutter close behind."—Moon-Priest Tedaza

name: Brimstone Nixad
description: The legend among the underworld explorers of the Undaunted is that these little incendiary sprites are responsible for lighting all the candles, torches, and lanterns found burning underground, flying ahead of adventurers to ignite them in the dark.

name: Brown Steeple Bat
description: "People blessed by these brown bat companions experience very few issues with insects. They love hiding in your pack during the day, and they'll keep you bug-free while you sleep at night."—Tanandra, Scholar-Errant

name: Cantaloupe Swamp Jelly
description: Though Argonians do relish the elastic flesh of the Black Marsh Swamp Jellies, the whimsical names they give them refer more to their appearance than to their flavor.

name: Carmine Wood Moth
description: Nearly driven to extinction a century ago by Nibenese, who used their brilliant ruby wing dust as rouge, these moths made a comeback in a different area: Valenwood. Friendly to a fault, they are now favored companions among alchemists.

name: Cipher's Eye Pocket Watcher
description: "What have you learned, Watcher? Mortals on Nirn keep small companions. Oh, is that so? Names you say? As my small companion, you wish one? Very well, I shall call you Ocula. You have indeed earned it."—Morian Zenas

name: Conjured Dragon Imp
description: This impressive vision is the work of a very dedicated illusion imp. The shimmering form sparks the adoration of all who see it, making for easy handouts and safe havens for this tiny so-called Dragon.

name: Crimson Torchbug
description: Khajiit claim these torchbugs are the light of Jode given form, which allows them to dance amid the moon-sugar cane and bless the crops. Now you can have one flitting about you! After all, having Jode's blessing is never a bad thing, right?

name: Crystaljack
description: These mesmerizing creatures hail from the Daedric realm of Mirrormoor. Unlike some of the other denizens of that realm, Crystaljacks appear to be organic in nature, with shimmering skin that simply mimics the appearance of mirrored surfaces.

name: Dappled Cactus Bat
description: "Sometimes called Friends of the Caravan, these black-and-white bats migrate among cacti stands in arid regions. Trackers follow their guano to find hydrating, safe cacti when in need. Easily trained to be a companion."—Tanandra, Scholar-Errant

name: Devoted Torchbug
description: The Wood Elves say that to be followed by a friendly Torchbug is an infallible sign of good fortune. Of course, they also catch them, dry them out, and smoke them in pipes.

name: Dockside Paper Wasp
description: "Clearing wasps from the Betnikh docks falls to our youngest warrior. One such asked a mage to help her befriend the wasps, and she led them away. All but one settled elsewhere, instead choosing to follow her loyally. I see you have one now."—Stulga

name: Duskfire Nectar Bat
description: "So colorful! And common around orchards, farms, and other places with cultivated fruit and flowers. A priceless companion for foragers and travelers since they can lead you to food."—Tanandra, Scholar-Errant

name: Dusklight Lunar Moth
description: Quiet, tree-shaded lakes attract these blue-purple moths. Legends claim they glide on starlight and rest upon the Moons' reflections in the water. If one follows you away, good luck is said to bless your path.

name: Emerald Oak Nixad
description: "Emerald Oak Nixads are known for their mischief. Their coloration allows them to hide in forests, waiting for unsuspecting travelers to pass by. Upon leaving, travelers will find their rations much lighter, especially sweets."—Gold Coast Field Guide

name: Evermore Painter's Moth
description: "Of course I used pigment from local moths when painting Duke Blaise Guimard's portrait. Several of my artist friends keep sanctuaries for these colorful creatures. Perhaps my own little Springrain will help start mine."—Lady Alyna Talemelier's Journal

name: Eyebright Raven
description: "The ravens of Rivenspire are some of the smartest in all of Tamriel. Something about surviving in such an inhospitable land, I think. This fine fellow has been my companion on many a long night in the study."—Lady Felyse Talemelier

name: Frostmoss Imp
description: "Why do people insist on having imps about? And why especially these kind? They twist whatever you tell them to do into something that serves them best, not you. Only those with an extraordinarily firm hand should even bother with them."—Divayth Fyr

name: Frostshriek Imp
description: "This devious little creature will drop the ambient temperature considerably when summoned. And mind your fingers—the little monster likes nothing better than to freeze them, break them off, and pop them into its mouth!"—Divayth Fyr

name: Galen Wisp
description: Wisps are sent from Y'ffre to herald the storms of Rain's Hand. To see one is to see the promise of new growth, new life, and a new chapter in nature's cycle.

name: Glimmergreen Dovah-Fly
description: "Respect the dovah-fly. They are the spirits of the ancestors given new life. They brighten the quiet tranquility of ponds and streams. What better afterlife is there?"—Druid Henneque Blakeley

name: Golden Eagle
description: "These majestic birds of prey are capable hunters, sighting their prey from great heights before descending in near silence for the kill. This prowess makes them prized by hunters and nobles alike."—Feathered Fauna, Translated

name: Green Dragon Imp
description: "Ha ha! Fooled you, didn't it? Looks just like a Baby Dragon, doesn't it? Well, there are no such things, and you should know better. It's just an Illusion Imp with a rather Peryite look to it. Baby Dragon, really!" —Abnur Tharn

name: Guild Conjured Wisp
description: "Look, it may not have much personality, but it's entrancing, in its own way. It's happy to see you, I think. The students at the Mages Guild were very proud of this conjuration. The least you can do is act impressed."—Mage Student Hrantin

name: Haunting Netch
description: "Gah! Netches! Mine kept getting stuck behind closed doors. So my friend and I made this ghostly netch. Yours for a song, five-claw! Not at all necromantic. Promise!"—Lanjo, merchant

name: Hearthhome Moth
description: These ponderous moths flap slowly between pools of moonlight, attracted by the glow. During the day, they either rest on shady tree trunks or follow behind those who make them feel safe. Their delicate wings are famously soft to the touch.

name: Heartwood Dauber
description: The wasps found in the heart of the woods around Lake Honrich use mud to build their nests. While they normally keep out of sight, they swarm any who threaten their nests. Those who help defend against intruders may just find a friend following them home.

name: Hollowjack Netch
description: The Witches Festival, which celebrates horror and death, also has a regrettable tradition of wanton vandalism associated with it, especially among Tamriel's callow youth. The so-called "Hollowjack Netch" appears to be a victim of this practice.

name: Ice Nixad
description: There is some debate among naturalists as to whether the Ice Nixad is a separate breed that is mainly seen in the winter because it hibernates during the warm months, or whether it's just a winter phase of ordinary Nixads that sometimes stays year-round.

name: Lemondot Netch
description: "Do colors seem louder? Does music taste different? Does Tirdas have a personality? You're probably experiencing the synesthesic venom of the rare lemondot netch. Relax. It's harmless. A little new perspective never killed anybody."—Alinon the Alchemist

name: Long-Winged Bat
description: Add this cute bat to your menagerie. Not only does it eat pesky bugs, but it'll keep you company on your adventures!

name: Mara's Blush Butterfly
description: Delicate in both form and color, this pink-hued butterfly flits around Elsweyr, Skyrim, Rivenspire—and around you! Tailor Medresi Grulathil looked to her own butterfly companion for inspiration while crafting ceremonial garb honoring Mara in Solitude.

name: Mead-Dancer Honeybee
description: "Bees are simple, really. They respect power. That's why they follow a queen. Just act like you're supposed to be in charge and they'll work for you. Show any weakness, any hesitation? That's when you get stung."—Hei Honey-Hands

name: Mint Swamp Jelly
description: Though the Argonians claim that they name each breed of Black Marsh Swamp Jelly for its hue rather than its taste, there's no denying that the Mint Jelly does have a gratifyingly refreshing flavor.

name: Monarch Butterfly
description: The migratory Monarch Butterfly is a common sight across all of southern Tamriel, and it's seen in the northern provinces during summer. The Monarch is said to represent the souls of the present, in contrast to the Ancestor Moth that represents the past.

name: Moorpecker Magpie
description: Few birds are as intelligent or vain as the Moorpecker Magpie. Prized by scholars and mages alike for their keen instincts and trainability, the birds can be huffy and prone to temper tantrums when not rewarded with shinies for their work.

name: Mossy Netch Calf
description: The greenish, or "Mossy" Netches, are most commonly found in the West Gash region of northwest Vvardenfell. The calves are docile, even for Netches, and will happily follow along behind anyone who smells of their favorite fungi.

name: Mustardseed Moth
description: Known for its brilliant yellow hues, this moth flits through the deciduous fall forests of Cyrodiil almost unseen. Each year, some fly beyond the Heartland's borders in all directions, as if trying to escape the war-torn province.

name: Nectarthief Nixad
description: The Nords absolutely loathe these particular nixads since they interfere with their bees—and thus mead production. In an effort to help, Solitude's Mages Guild trained them to take instruction, making them into companions. Need a drinking buddy?

name: Orchid Nixad
description: The rarest of these fay creatures is the Orchid Nixad, said to be sacred to the goddess Dibella, and found only in wild places hallowed to her worship. It's known that the Empress Tavia had an Orchid Nixad as a friend and companion.

name: Orchid Whisper Moth
description: The Dragonstar Caravan Company first found these brilliant moths while traveling from Evermore. Though attracted to the campfires, they didn't burn themselves. Instead, they settled on the caravan's goods, then followed them as if guarding them.

name: Passion Dancer Blossom
description: Allow the passion of Dibella to lead you in a dance of her choosing and, in return, she may gift you with boon of one of her lively blooms. These frolicsome flowers flourish in the presence of energetic adherents like you.

name: Pellucid Swamp Jelly
description: A favorite of veterinarians and beast masters across Tamriel, these netches are prized for their clear gelatinous outer membranes that allow students to view its organs from a distance.

name: Phoenix Moth
description: "Druids say the moths are ash made manifest. They leap from the flames of Mount Firesong and flutter away on the breeze. Nonsense! I've seen a moth ignite and then emerge from the coals like a cocoon."—Feather-Brained Teeska

name: Pink Torchbug
description: Some followers of Stendarr claim that those who see a Pink Torchbug must perform great acts of charity and mercy by sunset the following day. If they please Stendarr, the pleasant little creature might follow them for a time.

name: Plum Swamp Jelly
description: The Plum Swamp Jelly is the rarest of the so-called "Flavor" Jellies, and seeing one is considered by many Argonians to be a sign of good fortune. It's not at all unusual for an Argonian to wear a Plum Jelly's feeler as a "Good Luck Tentacle."

name: Pocket Watcher
description: "Some keep so-called Pocket Watchers as pets, playing off the name of those Pocket Mammoths seen in Wrothgar. Even at their smaller size? Still not the wisest move. Small Daedra are still Daedra, after all, and thus beyond our ken. "—Warlock Aldaale

name: Purple Torchbug
description: Madness follows the Purple Torchbug, or so some claim. Others believe that those who once held Sheogorath's attention attract these insects. Either way, perhaps Sheogorath's dubious blessing touched them.

name: Regal Dovah-Fly
description: Many a Vvardenfell youngster growing up in the swamps of West Gash or the Bitter Coast remembers spending happy hours playing "dodge-dovah" with these hovering bug-buddies! If hand-raised from larval form, they can become devoted companion animals.

name: Regal Dragon Imp
description: Those who have watched this particular imp's mimicry wonder how it survived seeing the Dragon that inspired its antics. Regardless, awe others by making this imp your companion.

name: Rosy Netch Calf
description: The reddish, or "Rosy" Netches are native to the foyadas of the Molag Amur region of Vvardenfell, where they live in a semi-wild state subject to the occasional round-ups of the Netchimen. The calves, sulfurous odor aside, are quite adorable.

name: Scintillant Dovah-Fly
description: The Dovah-Fly is a common sight in the oil-slick ravines of the Clockwork City. While its ornate clockworks are a wonder to behold, it's hard to shake the feeling that it's always watching you.

name: Screaming Midyear Nixad
description: "Why. Can't. They. Keep. Quiet? Arkay blesses them with their own cycle, but every few years they claw their way back into Greenshade. And what do they do once they get here? Scream. Constantly."—Hasinel, Lament of the Midyear Screech

name: Sea Sapphire Dovah-Fly
description: Often accompanying ships as they leave port, each blue-purple iridescent Dovah-Fly chooses a person to follow. Each night, the whirr of its gently flitting wings pull its chosen one to slumber, and at sunrise it lightly lands on its "pet" to wake them up.

name: Seht's Dovah-Fly
description: These are clearly fabricants, clockwork simulations of living creatures, with the distinctive appearance of the handiwork of Sotha Sil. But if so, how did they escape Clockwork City? What powers them? And why do they make such loyal pets? No one knows.

name: Senchal Horned Owl
description: "This one has always admired the owls around here. Very wise creatures. Most do not get too close, even when offered treats. Most, but not all. This is Hooty. A very clever name, yes? What else does one call a pet owl?"—Traveling Merchant J'margo

name: Sepulchral Swamp Jelly
description: "Things that sink in the swamp never truly leave the cold embrace of the muck. Their tormented ends infuse the very land itself, haunting and changing the few living creatures that survive in that wretched place."—Swamp Songs: A History

name: Shadowswift Bat
description: "Normally you don't see these black bats because they prefer caves and other areas avoided by people. However, if trained, these fellows consider you a member of their colony and hate to leave your side."—Tanandra, Scholar-Errant

name: Snow Throat Fruit Bat
description: "Pure white, these bats, making them hard to see in wintry conditions. But give one a bit of banana, and it'll stick close to you for a while. With a constant diet of bananas and other fruits? You are its boon companion."—Tanandra, Scholar-Errant

name: Soulfire Dragon Illusion
description: "After much knowledge-seeking, I learned to summon an illusion of a small, fiery Dragon to follow me. While it's not the same as the real thing, that endears me to it more. Who wants a real Dragon around, after all?"—Ninaleon Sightbinder the First

name: Springlight Moth
description: Originally from the Tenmar Jungle, these green moths spread via caravans and carry the scent of fresh spring rains with every flap of their wings.

name: Stainedwing Bat
description: The wings on these bats are mesmerizing, though difficult to spot during the day. When backlit by the light of Tamriel's moons, they seem to ignite in the sky. The illusion draws insects, a happy feast for the Stainedwing Bat.

name: Stainedwing Butterfly
description: Despite their magnificent and fragile appearance, these butterflies are quite resilient. They've been known to cling to their chosen master through thick and thin, even in the midst of battle.

name: Stoneglow Imp
description: "Don't let those icy blue eyes fool you. It's their claws you need to keep an eye on—they can shatter stone, leaving behind nothing but glowing rubble. Thankfully, they're actually quite good-natured creatures once they imprint on you."—Divayth Fyr

name: Stonewisp of Truth and Law
description: Mage faithful of Julianos create these unique creatures as a form of devotional art. The wisp represents orderly aesthetics, a sense of balance, and focused energy. It also makes for a beautiful focusing tone while meditating.

name: Swamp Jelly
description: Though obviously related to the netches of northeast Tamriel, the swamp jellies of southern Black Marsh also have a disquieting resemblance to aquatic jellyfish. Natural philosophers have no adequate explanation for this.

name: Sylvan Nixad
description: Once a common sight in Cyrodiil's Great Forest, the Sylvan Nixad is now most often encountered in the glades and meadows of the Gold Coast. Once tamed, they make charming companions, loyal and easy to care for.

name: Tenmar Magpie
description: Brilliant hues mark this vibrant magpie, whose primary habitat lies within the Tenmar Forest. Locals sometimes train them to signal the location of fallen prey for easier retrieval.

name: Tourmaline Swamp Jelly
description: The Argonian who named this multihued jelly claims inspiration from the mineral, though some note she was calling it a "watermelon jelly" first. Oddly enough, some find its flavor resembles that of the fruit.

name: Turquoise Nixad
description: Scholars think the iridescent blue Turquoise Nixad must have inherent magical properties, because those wings certainly aren't big enough to enable it to fly. Yet fly it does, flitting about like a beautiful human-shaped hummingbird moth.

name: Unstable Morpholith
description: "The instability inherent in the structure of some morpholiths makes them unsuitable for use as sigil stones, yet that doesn't stop certain Daedric Princes from trying. Imagine the surprise when said portals don't work."—Warlock Aldaale

name: Vampiric Dragon Imp
description: This imp, after being caged by Vampires, freed itself and can now join you in your journeys. Easily spooked, it often changes into a Vampiric Dragon form, hoping to seem fiercer than it is.

name: Vashabar Petal Moth
description: "I think Y'ffre has a lesson for us in all his creations. Moths especially. It's easy to overlook them. But they remind us how to be soft. How to move lightly through the world, and how to follow the light."—Gundelion of Vashabar

name: Vivec's Promise Butterfly
description: Like the Warrior-Poet himself, this striking butterfly is bisected by two distinct color palettes. The Tribunal's faithful consider it a good omen to see one of these creatures, and a blessing from Lord Vivec himself if one chooses to follow you.

name: White Butterfly
description: Template Description

name: White Torchbug
description: Some believe that gaining Meridia's favor is like gripping a double-edged blade tightly with bare hands. Yet, if you perform an action she likes, she may gift you with a White Torchbug—perhaps the least worrisome of her favors!

name: Witches Festival Ghost Netch
description: While it's unclear whether this little netch understands the nuances behind the Witches Festival's many traditions, its joyous tootling is reason enough to let it join in the celebrations.

name: Xylo Pollen Bat
description: These brown-furred bats pollinate flowers along the Xylo River. Without them, nature's web in the Valenwood would be deeply disrupted. Plus they look adorable when they sneeze.

name: Yoltoor Dovah-Fly
description: Shimmering like fire, these dovah-flies dart around port cities, eating many of the nuisance insects that pester transported livestock. Recently, merchants started training and selling them to help others with insect issues.

name: Aeonstone Formation
description: The unusual properties of the crystal known as aeonstone continue to confound alchemists and arcane researchers. This particular formation resonates with nearby inactive deposits, causing them to emit a soft glow.

name: Apocryphal Tome
description: This is a small house item.

name: Armory Station
description: You can place this station in multiple homes, where it allows you and your guests to save and equip Armory builds.

name: Augur of the Obscure
description: This headstrong crystal skull ignored your decision to give it away and elected to stay with you instead. It could tell you all about the sublime mysteries of creation, but would much rather rant, joke, and complain.

name: Behold Khunzar-ri's Ambition
description: Place on the Altar of Ambition in the Hall of the Lunar Champion to unlock a portal to Khunzar-ri's childhood home.

name: Behold Khunzar-ri's Betrayal
description: Place on the Altar of Betrayal in the Hall of the Lunar Champion to unlock an overlook of the Halls of Colossus.

name: Behold Khunzar-ri's Guile
description: Place on the Altar of Guile in the Hall of the Lunar Champion to unlock a long-forgotten corner of Moongrave Fane.

name: Behold the Lunar Champion
description: Place on the Jonelight Altar in the Hall of the Lunar Champion to awaken the lunar reflector.

name: Blackwood Tapestry
description: Exquisitely designed, this warm-hued tapestry of Blackwood serves as both an art piece and a practical guide to the region.

name: Chronometer of the Tribunal
description: You may place the Chronometer in your home. Watching the dial spin causes local perception of time to shift. Until the Chronometer is disturbed, time stands still. Enjoy Sotha Sil's morning sun, Almalexia's mid-day mercy, or the star-spun night of Vivec.

name: Dragon's Treasure Trove
description: You have claimed a share of the Dragon's Treasure Trove. Place it in your home, and show off your hard-earned riches.

name: Fan of False-Face
description: This fan allows its bearer to steal another's face; though at the cost of slowly losing themselves.

name: How to Scribe
description: Any who possess this tome have, at their fingertips, a comprehensive guide to the art of scribing spells.

name: Khajiit of the Moons Replica
description: A perfect replica of the priceless tapestry called Khajiit of the Moons.

name: Khunzar-ri's Rest
description: The Laughing Lion has taken a liking to you! Place this ancient sarcophagus in your home and his carefree wisdom will always be close to hand.

name: Kynareth's Icon of Storm Control
description: After placing this furnishing in your home, a quick prayer to Kynareth causes the weather around you to change. Until you use the vessel again, the skies remain in their current state. Homes without skies are not impacted by this furnishing.

name: Lady Garick's Sacred Shield
description: Lady Joslin Garick brought her crew home safely until the last time—or so the legends state. Now that you have proven worthy of her heritage, you can hang this famous All Flags Navy captain's shield on your wall.

name: Music Box, Oath of the Keepers
description: When activated, plays a music box arrangement of the profound "Oath of the Keepers" composition.

name: Painting: All Flags on High
description: A painting featuring Gonfalon Bay nestled among its protective waters and cliffs, with a mysterious knight overlooking it all.

name: Painting: Arrival at Bal Foyen
description: The light of dawn caresses the spires of Bal Foyen as a trader and their travel-burdened guar arrive at this Dark Elf sanctum by the sea.

name: Painting: Baron Zaudrus Triumphs
description: A painting of the Havocrel named Baron Zaudrus, defeating those who oppose him.

name: Painting: Dagon's Mercy
description: A painting of Mehrunes Dagon, towering over his cultists in the Deadlands.

name: Painting: Galen in Harmony
description: A painting presenting a peaceful blending of Breton and druidic architecture, set against the wild lushness of Galen's flora.

name: Painting: Infinite Archive
description: "Those whom Hermaeus Mora calls to the Infinite Archive may serve him—or may choose to leave. But who, upon understanding the limitless knowledge they may access, dares refuse the Lord of Secrets without feeling bereft forever after?"—Mage Allierwen

name: Painting: Leyawiin Awaits
description: A painting of Leyawiin, the Nibenese city standing at the mouth of the Niben River and known for its majestic chapel honoring Zenithar.

name: Painting: Lucent Citadel
description: Shrouded in mystery, the Lucent Citadel gleams in the sand of Fargrave's wastelands.

name: Painting: Oathsworn Pit
description: A painting of Oathsworn Pit, where followers of Malacath train in three different forms of combat.

name: Painting: Sanity's Edge
description: "As you can see by my attached references, I am one of the foremost experts in vicinage wards, forfending spells, and the art of research. If anyone can deal with the Dreamstone's ire, it is me. I hope you come to the same conclusion."—Warlock Vanton

name: Painting: Shadowfen Mirescape
description: "You may see a swamp. Ruins. Trees. Water. But I see life and endings. Death and beginnings. And most of all change. Learn from the Shadowfen as I do."—Juutenma, Shadowscale

name: Painting: Systres Archipelago
description: A painting by Vaudrie Barthel, well-known for her landscapes and scenes depicting life and nature in the Systres Isles.

name: Painting: Systres Seaside Manor
description: A painting by Vaudrie Barthel that captures the play of light and water at an elegant manor in the Systres Archipelago.

name: Painting: The Endless Library
description: A painting depicting just one of the innumerable studies within the Endless Library of Hermaeus Mora.

name: Painting: The Gates of Brass
description: A painting of the Brass Fortress, seat of power for the Clockwork God, Sotha Sil.

name: Painting: The Stitches
description: Located within the Scar in Northern Elsweyr, the Stitches draws the eye of many an artist seeking the challenge of illustrating a more vertically oriented settlement.

name: Replica Rithana-di-Renada
description: A perfect replica of the Rithana-di-Renada, complete with the ancient Song of Kingdoms.

name: Replica Zenithar Adytum Gate
description: A perfect replica of the Adytum Gate from the Zenithar Abbey.

name: Replica of the Xinchei-Konu
description: This meticulous reproduction of the ancient Argonian calendar may not have the storied history of the original, but is a masterpiece of stonework in its own right.

name: Revolving Celestiodrome
description: A gift from the mysterious Sotha Sil himself, this device displays the superb craftsmanship and meticulous detail that are hallmarks of the work of the Clockwork God.

name: Sacred Hourglass of Alkosh
description: You may place the hourglass within your home. Focusing on its falling sands causes them to blur, and local perception of time to shift. Until the hourglass is disturbed, time seems to stand still. Enjoy everything from eternal sunrises to endless nights.

name: Senche-raht Statue, Battle-Bound
description: "Oh, yes! I've seen legionaries stand their ground against a battle-bonded Khajiit pair. Never seen one survive the experience, but you've got to respect anyone who faces a Senche-raht and their chosen battlemate." —Nallangaer, Vinedusk Ranger

name: Statue of Gloria
description: Granted to the winner of the 2020 Tamriel Together Sweepstakes.

name: Statue, Ascendant Lord
description: Though the artist who sculpted this statue remains unknown, those who have faced the Ascendant Lord declare it captures this leader's might and presence perfectly. Claimed from the treasure trove of the Ascendant Order.

name: Statuette: Alessia, Liberator
description: A miniature statue of Alessia, the liberator of the humans of Cyrodiil.

name: Statuette: Ascendant Lord
description: A miniature statue of the mysterious Ascendant Lord, who seeks to claim an ancient legacy.

name: Statuette: Auri-El and Xarxes
description: A miniature statue of Auri-El and Xarxes, based on the statues in the Monastery of Serene Harmony in Shimmerene.

name: Statuette: Auri-El, Aldmer King
description: A miniature statue of Auri-El, chief deity of the Aldmeri pantheon, with an eagle.

name: Statuette: Auriel of Garlas Agea
description: A miniature statue of Auriel, King of the Aldmer. Based on the storied effigy of the same name in the ruins of Garlas Agea along the Gold Coast.

name: Statuette: Azura, Moon and Star
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Azura, bearing Moon and Star sigils.

name: Statuette: Baron-Admiral Olo
description: A miniature statue of Bendu Olo, Baron-Admiral of the All Flags Navy, as sculpted in High Isle.

name: Statuette: Boethra, Orkha-Bane
description: A miniature statue of Boethra and feline companion, a banisher of the demon Orkha.

name: Statuette: Child of the Sky
description: A miniature statue of a Nord skald with hawk and horn.

name: Statuette: Clavicus Vile, Masque
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Clavicus Vile, holding aloft his Masque.

name: Statuette: Dancing Tojay
description: A miniature statue of a Tojay Khajiit, dancing in celebration.

name: Statuette: Dibella, Blessed Lady
description: A miniature statue of the Divine Dibella, the Lady of Love, Beauty, Art, and Music.

name: Statuette: Duchess Martinne
description: A miniature statue of the Duchess Martinne Guimard, leader of the consortium that purchased the Systres Archipelago.

name: Statuette: Dwemer Guardian
description: A miniature statue of a sentinel found outside many Dwarven ruins in Morrowind.

name: Statuette: High Elf Mage
description: "Some claim to know the provenance of this sleek piece of art, but they know nothing. Especially when it comes to how impressive your home would be with a replica in it!" —Zaidrashi, Merchant

name: Statuette: Hircine, the Huntsman
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Hircine, the Huntsman.

name: Statuette: Hortator Nerevar
description: A miniature statue of the Hortator Nerevar

name: Statuette: Imperial Knight
description: A miniature statue of an Imperial knight, standing proud and ready to serve.

name: Statuette: Imperial Warrior
description: Discipline and resolution. Protection and honor. These traits and more embody the spirit of the Imperial warrior. Display these noble qualities in this artful statuette!

name: Statuette: Kaalgrontiid
description: A miniature statue of Kaalgrontiid, the emerald sovereign of wrath and terror.

name: Statuette: Kaladas of Leyawiin
description: A miniature statue of Saint Kaladas, builder of the Great Chapel of Zenithar in Leyawiin.

name: Statuette: Kinlord Nemfarion
description: A miniature statue of Kinlord Nemfarion, founder of Corgrad on Summerset Isle.

name: Statuette: Kynareth of the Winds
description: A miniature statue of Kynareth, goddess of the elements, as sculpted in High Isle.

name: Statuette: Kynareth, Air Goddess
description: A miniature statue of Kynareth, Divine patron of sailors and travelers.

name: Statuette: Malacath, Furious One
description: "Hold your grudges well. Keep them close to your heart. Let them punctuate every blow you make as you fulfill upon your promise of vengeance. And display this statue in your dwelling so that all may know the cost of crossing you."—Lucky Lashgikh

name: Statuette: Malacath, Orc-Father
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Malacath, the Orc-Father.

name: Statuette: Mane, Moons-Blessed
description: A miniature statue depicting one of the Manes, the spiritual leaders of the Khajiit.

name: Statuette: Mehrunes Dagon
description: A miniature statue of Mehrunes Dagon, Daedric Prince of Destruction and Ambition.

name: Statuette: Mephala, Webspinner
description: A miniature statue of Mephala, the Daedric Prince of Secrets and Murder.

name: Statuette: Meridia, Bright Lady
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Meridia, the Bright Lady.

name: Statuette: Mermaid of Anvil
description: A miniature version of the enigmatic mermaid statue found in Anvil.

name: Statuette: Molag Bal, the Brutal
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Molag Bal, Lord of Brutality.

name: Statuette: Mora, Lord of Secrets
description: All statues of the Inevitable Knower are, after a fashion, access points from Apocrypha to Nirn. Given that, go carefully as you invite Hermaeus Mora into your home.

name: Statuette: Morwha, Desire's Root
description: A miniature statue of Morwha, the Yokudan goddess of fertility and love.

name: Statuette: Nocturnal, Gloamqueen
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Nocturnal, the Night Mistress.

name: Statuette: Orc Warrior
description: A miniature statue of an Orc warrior emanating strength.

name: Statuette: Peryite, Blightlord
description: A miniature statue of Peryite, the Daedric Prince of Pestilence.

name: Statuette: Peryite, Taskmaster
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Peryite, the Taskmaster.

name: Statuette: Pride of Alkosh Hero
description: A miniature statue of a hero of the Pride of Alkosh, standing triumphantly over her foe.

name: Statuette: Prince Hew
description: A miniature statue of the Yokudan Prince Hew, who is also known as Prince Hubalajad.

name: Statuette: Redguard Warrior
description: A miniature statue of a Redguard warrior, often used within royal tombs.

name: Statuette: Revered Night Mother
description: A miniature statue of the Night Mother, worshiped by the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Statuette: Sai Sahan, Deliverer
description: A miniature statue of Sai Sahan, the liberator of Leyawiin.

name: Statuette: Sanguine
description: A miniature statue of Daedric Prince Sanguine, hoisting a tankard during a revelry.

name: Statuette: Scion of Bal
description: A miniature statue of the Scion of Bal

name: Statuette: Senche-raht
description: A miniature statue of a Senche-raht Khajiit and its chosen battlemate.

name: Statuette: Sheogorath, the Mad
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Sheogorath, the Mad God.

name: Statuette: Sithis, Dread Lord
description: A miniature statue of Sithis, patron of the Dark Brotherhood.

name: Statuette: Son of Skyrim
description: A miniature statue of a Son of Skyrim

name: Statuette: Sotha Sil, Tinkerer
description: A miniature statue of Sotha Sil, the Clockwork God.

name: Statuette: Steadfast Stendarr
description: A miniature statue of the Divine Stendarr, God of Mercy, Justice, and Charity.

name: Statuette: Suthay, Nimble Bishop
description: A miniature statue of a Suthay furstock Moon-Bishop.

name: Statuette: Syrabane, the Warlock
description: A miniature statue of Syrabane, an Aldmeri god-ancestor of magic.

name: Statuette: Telvanni Magister
description: A miniature statue of a Telvanni Mage, carved to venerate a Magister long past but not forgotten.

name: Statuette: Trinimac, Paragon
description: A miniature statue of the divine warrior Trinimac, holding aloft a sword.

name: Statuette: Vaermina, Dreamweaver
description: A miniature statue of the Daedric Prince Vaermina, the Lady of Nightmares.

name: Statuette: Vivec's Triumph
description: A miniature version of the "Thirty-Fourth Sermon" statue, carved by the people of Necrom.

name: Statuette: Vivec, Warrior-Poet
description: A miniature statue of the living god Lord Vivec, Warrior-Poet.

name: Statuette: Wolf and Warrior
description: A miniature statue of a Nord warrior with his wolf companion.

name: Statuette: Yokudan War-Scholar
description: Brilliant battlefield tacticians often became venerated heroes among the Yokudan warriors.

name: Statuette: Zenithar, God of Toil
description: A miniature statue of Zenithar, holding an anvil.

name: Tales of Tribute Decks, Display
description: A perfect display case for your perfect decks! What more can you ask for other than victory?

name: Tales of Tribute Table, Display
description: Set up your home's gaming room properly with this exquisite Tales of Tribute table. This table does not allow you to play Tales of Tribute matches.

name: Vvardenfell Scale Model
description: Librarian Bradyn presented you with this scale model of the island of Vvardenfell—a miniature version of the replica in the library in Vivec City.

name: Adorable Assassin
description: Knock 'em dead with this casual hairstyle popularized by the Dark Elf assassins of Morrowind.

name: Anterior Antlers
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Arcanist's Crest
description: An uncomplicated style to keep you looking good whether you're searching the stacks of Apocrypha or delving for esoteric knowledge in the depths of a dungeon. Wear it with pride, Arcanist.

name: Assassin-Style Sunset Crest
description: This season the hairstyles of the Morag Tong are all the rage—even among the usually Dark Elf-averse Argonians!

name: Azure Ombre
description: "Why did I choose this stunning blue hair style? First, it's my choice! Second, if you can do this, you're a master alchemist and hair artist like me. Why not flaunt it?"—Dabienne Geontene of Skingrad This hair style overrides your base hair color.

name: Balding But Distinguished
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Barbaric Windblown Hair
description: At last, a hairstyle that expresses the wild, windblown freedom of the untamed barbarian warrior. When you've spent all day galloping across the wilderness in pursuit of loot and adventure, THIS is what your hair looks like!

name: Beaded Crested Dreads
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Beaded Dreadacles
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Bedhead Bob
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Braided Ponytail
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Braided Tresses
description: About to leap into battle? Or pirouette into a gala? Do so knowing that you are both well-coiffed and richly accessorized.

name: Breton Tonsure
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Broad Web Ears
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Bruma Burr Cut
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: By Kyne, It's Humid
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Carnaval Side Part
description: Join the celebration with a festive makeover for your crowning glory! Ornate hairpieces add a bit of flash to what's already a stunning look.

name: Center-Part Long
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Center-Part Medium
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Central Spine Crest
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Coil with Long Fall
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Coil with Ring Braids
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Coiled Bob
description: "Derik Hallin of the mid-First Era popularized tightly coiled short hair, specifically among sword-singers. Since then, some among us who study the Book of Circles created variants for Khajiit and Argonians who wish to learn our ways."—Khazha of Sentinel

name: Color Streaked River Braid
description: It's as if a master painter touched your tresses—or you fell down among the dye pots in a dyeing station! Either way, the result is fabulous.

name: Covenant Lizard-Plumes
description: Going to war may mean donning a helm, but beneath it an Argonian Covenant warrior is entitled to wear these official Alliance Lizard-Plumes, which keep out of a helmet's way while still looking superb.

name: Covenant War-Locks
description: Going to war may mean donning a helm, but beneath it an honored Covenant warrior is entitled to wear these official Alliance War-Locks, which keep long hair under control while still looking superb.

name: Cranial Spine Cluster
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Crest with Pony Braid
description: This topknot crest descending into a triple-wrapped braided ponytail is both warlike and practical, and is often worn by those soldiers who worship Alkosh, the Dragon-Cat.

name: Crested Shag Mullet
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Curly Back Bun
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Curly Mane
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Cutting Edge
description: Your tongue isn't the only sharp thing about you—your keen coif can slice right through the pompous bluster of even the stodgiest get-together.

name: Daedra Horns with Spike Cluster
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Dominion Lizard-Locks
description: Going to war may mean donning a helm, but beneath it an Argonian Dominion warrior is entitled to wear these official Alliance Lizard-Locks, which keep beaded bristles under control while still looking superb.

name: Dominion War-Locks
description: Going to war may mean donning a helm, but beneath it an honored Dominion warrior is entitled to wear these official Alliance War-Locks, which keep long hair under control while still looking superb.

name: Don't Touch My Pigtails
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Draping Locks
description: "Veya's a practical child. While others her age favor short hair or intricate braids, she merely tucks her hair behind her ears and gets on with the task at hand. She'll excel at whatever she wants."—Vilyn Hlas, tutor employed by Councilor Eris

name: Dread Turban Bun
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Dreadmax Ponytail
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Dual Forehead Horns
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Dual Hind Horns
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Feathered Headdress
description: Why bother with spines or spikes when your skull can sprout a fountain of feathers? You'll be the fanciest lizard in the mud-wallow.

name: Feathered Kelp-Scalp
description: Seaweed head-feathers were first popularized by the aquatic hunter Lurks-in-Murk of Helstrom.

name: Fine Upstanding Spines
description: Erect the spines of high fashion! And add in a couple of upturned petite nose horns to seal the deal. Xuth!

name: Fluttering Forehead Feathers
description: "As an archer, I like to have a windvane right on my noggin" says Tlaxal-Hei of Thorn.

name: Fore-and-Aft Webbed Spike Crest
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Four Sheathed Spikes
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Frisee Pouffee
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Geyser Ponytail
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Herd of Ponies
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Heroic Hind Braid
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Heroic Pony Dreads
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: High Elven Instigator
description: "Oh this look? I think it suits me. It's gotten me into ballrooms, estates, even the odd castle. I'm not one to kiss and tell, but if you stick around we can talk about some kissing I've been involved in."—Tanlorin

name: Keen-Edged Shag
description: Those who work in the shadows need hairstyles as sharp as their blades. With this no-fuss shag cut, you're quickly set for your latest assignation or assassination.

name: Left-Parted Bob
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Left-Parted Cropped
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Leftside Bun Twist
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Lizard Rhinoceros
description: Even more legendary than the unicorn is that imaginary two-horned beast called the rhinoceros. Live the legend with Lizard Rhinoceros horns!

name: Long Beaded Mane
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Cornrows
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Crested Dreads
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Curly Crown Braid
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Elven Braid
description: There's always been a lot of cultural interchange between the Wood Elves and the Catfolk, and it even shows up in their hairstyles, as in the popular Long Elven Braid style.

name: Long Foregathered Mane
description: This feline warriors' favorite consists of a handsome long mane, gathered in three places by turquoise-studded pewter clasps. Fierce but not entirely informal.

name: Long Full Dreads
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Hind Braid
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Matted Mane
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Pulled-Back Pony
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Rightside Bang
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Long Wild Locks
description: Who's got the hair that drives 'em wild when playing tavern bard at the inn? You do.

name: Long and Combed Back
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Magenta Rainbow Hair
description: Show your pride in your hair, mane, or bristles with this shimmering rainbow that veers into the ultraviolet.

name: Management Material
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Mane-of-Many-Rivers
description: This hairstyle honors the goddess Khenarthi in her agricultural aspect as The Gatherer of Waters.

name: Maximum Frisee
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.

name: Maximum Ponytail
description: One of the standard hairstyles available at every Tamrielic salon.
